tasks.title: Remember a neighbour that had the whole press budget, report deferred remembered files as skipped, and never restart a live worker
tasks.dod: A file whose check started with the press's whole budget (no earlier file in this press spent any) and still could not be judged is remembered as timed out (same `NeighbourKey`), whether the listing or the probe ran out; only a file cut short because earlier files spent the budget stays unremembered and unreported.; When the target is chosen after remembered files that come before it in scan order were deferred, each such file is published as `FileSkipped(name, "unreadable")`, logged and counted in `checked N`; the terminal and the note show it as for any skip.; The abandoned worker `Task` (listing or probe) is kept per `NeighbourKey`; while it has not completed, a later press steps past that file (counted as checked, reason `unreadable`) without starting a new worker, and retries only once the task completed or the key changed.; Tests: listing 1.2 s + probe 1.9 s on E2 → press 2 reaches E3 (and reports E2 skipped); a remembered E2 deferred before E3 → press 2 publishes `FileSkipped(E2, unreadable)` and `checked` counts it; a listing that never returns + three presses → exactly one `ListTracks` call for E2.; spec §6.1 (:247 and :249), sad.md §7 (:526) and cli.md §2.2 (:85) state the final rule: what is remembered, that the 3 s budget counts from the start of the command plus any queue wait, that remembered files are reported as skipped, and that a live worker is not restarted (so at most one blocked thread per file).; `dotnet build DualPlayer.slnx` (warnings are errors), `dotnet test DualPlayer.slnx` and `dotnet format DualPlayer.slnx --verify-no-changes` clean

tasks.title: Let a stepped-past neighbour play once it recovers, judge the whole budget per press, report a remembered file once, and keep probe workers too
tasks.dod: A file stepped past because its worker (listing or probe) is still running is reported skipped (reason `unreadable`, counted in `checked N`) for that press only: it is written neither to `_judged` nor removed from `_timedOut`, and once its worker has completed the next press checks it again (completed `_workers` entries are pruned). This also holds for a healthy file whose cut listing is still running.; "Whole budget" is decided by a per-press flag (no earlier file in this press started a check), not by elapsed time since `scanAt`, so the folder enumeration, sort and stats never count against it; the post-listing exit (too little left for the probe) sets `timedOut = wholeBudget`.; A remembered file is reported skipped at most once per press: the block after the target reports only remembered files that were deferred and not visited in this press.; The abandoned probe worker is kept per `NeighbourKey` (or per path inside `FfmpegPictureProbe`) like the listing worker: while it runs, no press starts another probe on that file; the file is stepped past as in the first box. At most one blocked thread per file, listing or probe.; Tests: (1) E2 only neighbour, listing blocked through press 2, released, press 3 plays E2; (2) a healthy E3 whose cut listing is still running at press 2 plays on press 3; (3) a folder listing that costs 200 ms of fake time, then E2 listing 1.2 s + probe 1.9 s → E2 remembered, press 2 reaches E3; (4) E2 listing 2.95 s → remembered; (5) the three-press sequence where E2 hangs again on press 3 and E3 plays → exactly one `FileSkipped(E2)` and `skipped 1`; (6) a probe that never returns + three presses → exactly one `Probe` call on E2. Each fails if its fix is reverted.; spec §6.1 (:249), sad §7 (:533) and cli.md §2.2 (:85) state the final rule: what is remembered, that the 3 s budget counts from when the session starts the command (a queue wait is not part of it), that remembered files are checked last and reported as skipped once, and that a live listing or probe worker is not restarted and its file plays once it recovers.; `dotnet build DualPlayer.slnx` (warnings are errors), `dotnet test DualPlayer.slnx` and `dotnet format DualPlayer.slnx --verify-no-changes` clean
